reminder-create.description: Create one durable Slack reminder. Convert the user's requested time to a future RFC3339 timestamp including its UTC offset before calling. If a date, time, or timezone is ambiguous, ask the user instead of guessing. The reminder will be sent in this conversation and mention the requesting user.

parameters.run_at: Future RFC3339 time with a timezone offset, e.g. 2026-07-15T18:30:00+08:00.
parameters.message: Short description of what to remind the user about.

reminder-list.description: List the requesting user's pending reminders.

reminder-cancel.description: Cancel one of the requesting user's pending reminders. Use reminder-list first if the reminder ID is unknown.

parameters.id: Reminder ID returned by reminder-create or reminder-list.

code-search.description: Search code with ripgrep under an allowed workspace root. Prefer this for symbols, error messages, routes, config keys, or string patterns in the local working tree. For broad investigations, narrow by repo/path/glob before expanding.

parameters.query: Literal string or regex pattern for ripgrep.
parameters.path: Directory or file under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.
parameters.glob: Optional rg glob filter, for example '*.go' or '!vendor'.
parameters.limit: Maximum matching lines. Defaults to 50, max 200.

code-read_file.description: Read a text file from an allowed workspace root. Use start_line and max_lines for large files. Read targeted ranges before making claims about file contents.

parameters.path: File path under one of WORKSPACE_ROOTS.
parameters.max_lines: Maximum lines to return. Defaults to 240, max 1000.

git-status.description: Read git branch and working tree status. This is read-only.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.

git-fetch_ref.description: Fetch origin and resolve a branch to an immutable commit ref without changing the working tree. Use this before git-search_ref or git-read_file_ref.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.
parameters.branch: Branch to resolve. If omitted, tries the configured default branch, main, then master.

git-search_ref.description: Search code at a git ref without changing the working tree. Use this instead of code-search when analyzing a specific branch or commit. Required before claiming that a specific guard, conditional, or log string exists at a particular ref.

parameters.ref: Immutable ref returned by git-fetch_ref, usually a commit SHA.
parameters.limit: Maximum matching lines. Defaults to 50, max 200.

git-read_file_ref.description: Read a file at a git ref without changing the working tree. Use before quoting code blocks or line numbers at a specific ref.

parameters.ref: Immutable ref returned by git-fetch_ref, usually a commit SHA.
parameters.max_lines: Maximum lines to return. Defaults to 240, max 1000.

git-log.description: Read recent commit history from a refreshed remote branch snapshot. This is read-only and does not checkout branches.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.
parameters.branch: Optional remote branch name. Pass this when the user asks about a specific branch's latest commits.

git-show.description: Show a commit diff or file content at a git revision. This is read-only.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.
parameters.rev: Commit SHA, branch, tag, or ref.

codegraph-overview.description: Build a lightweight Go code graph for a refreshed git branch snapshot. Use for architecture orientation before reading specific files.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.
parameters.limit: Maximum packages and edges to show. Defaults to 40, max 120.

codegraph-dependencies.description: Show internal imports and importers for one Go package in a refreshed git branch snapshot.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.
parameters.package: Package import path, directory, name, or unique fragment.

codegraph-callers.description: Find simple Go call sites for a function or method name in a refreshed git branch snapshot. Treat as a static hint and confirm with source reads.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.

github-dispatch_workflow.description: Trigger a GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch run. When the user's request is clear and specific, execute directly without asking for a separate confirmation. Ask only for missing required inputs.

parameters.repository: GitHub repository in owner/repo form. Defaults to configured repository when set.
parameters.workflow: Workflow file name, ID, or configured alias.
parameters.ref: Git ref in the workflow repository, usually main.
parameters.inputs: workflow_dispatch inputs as key-value pairs. Pass values exactly as requested by the user.

github-workflow_runs.description: List recent GitHub Actions workflow runs. Use after triggering a workflow or when the user asks about CI/CD status.

parameters.repository: GitHub repository in owner/repo form. Defaults to configured repository when set.
parameters.workflow: Workflow file name, ID, or configured alias.
parameters.limit: Maximum runs to return. Defaults to 5, max 20.

github-pr_diff.description: Fetch GitHub pull request metadata and unified diff for review or investigation.

parameters.repository: GitHub repository in owner/repo form. Defaults to configured repository when set.

github-job_logs.description: Fetch GitHub Actions job logs for a workflow run or specific job. When the user provides a GitHub Actions URL, pass it as url directly; do not manually retype IDs unless needed. Lists all jobs in the run and fetches logs for failed jobs. Supports pagination: defaults to showing the last 200 lines (tail) where test results typically appear. Call again with different start_line to browse other sections.

parameters.repository: GitHub repository in owner/repo form. Defaults to configured repository when set.
parameters.url: GitHub Actions run or job URL. Prefer this when the user pasted a URL; repository, run_id, and job_id are extracted automatically.
parameters.run_id: Workflow run ID from the GitHub Actions URL (the number after /actions/runs/).
parameters.job_id: Optional specific job ID. If omitted, logs for all failed jobs in the run are returned.
parameters.start_line: 1-based start line. Negative values count from end (e.g. -500 shows last 500 lines). Defaults to tail (last max_lines lines).
parameters.max_lines: Maximum lines to return per page. Defaults to 200, max 500.

shell.description: Run a read-only shell command for operational inspection. Supports pipelines with | for idiomatic one-liners like "kubectl get pods -n mt-prod | grep Crash" or "git log --oneline | head -20". Allowed programs: git (all read subcommands), kubectl (get/describe/logs/top/rollout/config/explain/version), gcloud (logging read, container/run/compute/artifacts/monitoring list/describe), gh (run/pr/issue/workflow list and view), helm (list/status/history/get/show), plus Unix utilities (grep, rg, jq, awk, sed, cat, head, tail, find, wc, sort, uniq, cut, tr, curl, date, echo, df, du, ps). Shell meta-operators && ; & > >> are blocked; | only.

parameters.command: The shell command to run. Supports pipelines. Examples: "kubectl get pods -n mt-prod | grep -v Running", "gcloud logging read 'severity>=ERROR' --project=my-proj --freshness=1h --limit=20", "git -C /path/to/repo log --oneline -20", "helm list -n default | grep -v DEPLOYED".

skills-load.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill by name. Call this before following that skill's workflow. Do not assume skill instructions until this tool returns them.

parameters.name: Skill name from the Available skills list.

delegate-run.description: Run a focused delegate for bounded analysis using only supplied context. Delegates cannot call tools or read files directly; they analyze only what you provide.

parameters.task: Specific question or analysis task for the delegate.
parameters.context: Evidence and context the delegate may use. Include relevant code, logs, or tool output.

explore-code.description: Launch a read-only code exploration sub-agent for genuinely broad investigations spanning multiple services or unclear ownership. Do NOT use for simple lookups (feature flags, config checks, single-function reads, API routes) — use code-search/code-read_file directly instead. The sub-agent runs in isolation and returns a summarized report which may lose nuance; always verify critical details from its report with targeted reads before citing them.

parameters.task: Specific investigation question for the read-only explorer.
parameters.boundaries: Known repo/root, branch/ref, service, feature surface, candidate files, or constraints. Include what has already been ruled out when useful.

knowledge-runbook_search.description: Search local runbooks for operational procedures, ownership, known alerts, dashboards, and escalation paths.

parameters.query: Service, alert, symptom, dashboard, or runbook search term.
parameters.limit: Maximum runbook matches. Defaults to 5, max 20.

plan-update.description: Create or update the current execution plan for a complex multi-step task. Use proactively for substantial coding, debugging, architecture review, broad comparison, or any request with 3+ meaningful steps. Do not use for trivial one-step lookups.

parameters.items: Ordered task list. Keep each item concrete, outcome-oriented, and small enough to finish or verify.
parameters.items.items: One task in the ordered plan.
parameters.items.items.id: Short stable identifier, such as 1, 2, or verify.
parameters.items.items.status: One of pending, in_progress, completed, blocked. Keep at most one item in_progress.
parameters.items.items.note: Optional blocker, verification result, or important detail.
parameters.summary: Optional short reason for this plan update.

code-symbols.description: Search symbols using language-server code intelligence. More precise than text search for finding functions, methods, classes, and interfaces. This is read-only.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.

code-definition.description: Find the definition for the symbol at a source position using language-server code intelligence. This is read-only.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.
parameters.path: Source file path inside the repo.

code-references.description: Find all references for the symbol at a source position using language-server code intelligence. This is read-only.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.
parameters.path: Source file path inside the repo.

code-diagnostics.description: Read language-server diagnostics (errors, warnings) for a source file. This is read-only and based on the current working tree.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.
parameters.path: Source file path inside the repo.

repo-search.description: Fetch a repository on demand, pin the requested branch to a commit snapshot, then search code at that snapshot. Prefer this for repository investigations involving a named branch/ref.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.
parameters.branch: Branch to analyze. If omitted, tries the configured default branch, main, then master.
parameters.limit: Maximum matching lines. Defaults to 50, max 200.

repo-read_file.description: Fetch a repository on demand, pin the requested branch to a commit snapshot, then read a file at that snapshot. Prefer this for repository file reads involving a named branch/ref.

parameters.repo: Repository path under WORKSPACE_ROOTS. Defaults to first root.
parameters.branch: Branch to analyze. If omitted, tries the configured default branch, main, then master.
parameters.max_lines: Maximum lines to return. Defaults to 240, max 1000.

gcp-logs.description: Query GCP Cloud Logging. This is read-only. Project, namespace, and service are per-call inputs; configured GCP values are only defaults, not fixed environments.

parameters.severity: Minimum severity, for example ERROR, WARNING, or INFO.
parameters.namespace: GKE namespace. Optional; when omitted, no namespace filter is added unless filter already contains one.
parameters.service: Service, deployment, or container name hint. Matched against common GKE labels.
parameters.freshness: Freshness window, for example 30m or 2h. Defaults to 30m.
parameters.limit: Maximum log entries. Defaults to 30, max 200.
parameters.project: GCP project. Defaults to configured GCP_PROJECT only when omitted.
parameters.format: Output format: json or value. Defaults to json.

diagnostics-incident_brief.description: Create a structured incident diagnostic brief from service, environment, symptom, and time window. Use this to plan an investigation before reading logs or code.

parameters.service: Service, deployment, job, or repository name.
parameters.symptom: Observed problem, alert, error, or regression.
parameters.window: Approximate time window, for example 30m, since deploy, or today.

diagnostics-timeline.description: Build an incident timeline from observed events. Use after collecting context from Slack, logs, deploys, or workflow runs.

parameters.title: Short incident or investigation title.
parameters.events: Timeline entries. Each item can include time, source, event, impact, and evidence.

diagnostics-evidence_board.description: Create a structured evidence board that separates facts, hypotheses, risks, and next checks. Use before giving a final incident answer to organize your findings.

parameters.facts: Verified facts with source or tool references.
parameters.hypotheses: Hypotheses with confidence level or disconfirming evidence.

notion-search.description: Search Notion pages or databases for incident notes, runbooks, and knowledge base entries.

notion-get_page.description: Read the full text content of a Notion page by ID or URL (app.notion.com or notion.so). Use this for any Notion link — it handles authentication via the configured PAT.

parameters.page_id: Notion page ID (UUID) or full Notion page URL (app.notion.com or notion.so).
parameters.depth: How many levels of nested blocks to expand. Defaults to 2, max 4.

notion-query_database.description: Query a Notion database with optional filters and sorts. Use to look up structured records such as incident history, on-call schedules, or known issues.

parameters.database_id: Database ID or URL. Defaults to the configured NOTION_DATABASE_ID when omitted.
parameters.filter: Notion filter object (see Notion API docs). Optional.
parameters.sorts: Array of Notion sort descriptors. Optional.
parameters.limit: Maximum rows to return. Defaults to 20, max 100.

youtrack-get_issue.description: Fetch an issue tracker issue by ID, including summary, description, state, assignee, and recent comments.

youtrack-search.description: Search the issue tracker using its query syntax.

slack-ask_user.description: Ask the Slack user for missing information, then pause the current run. Use only when one concrete missing constraint blocks the next deterministic step. Name the missing repo, path, branch, environment, account, catalog, parameter, config, permission, channel, or data source.

parameters.question: Specific question to ask in the current thread.

slack-file_search.description: Search an uploaded Slack text or PDF file by file ID and return relevant excerpts. Use when the initial file excerpt is truncated or the file is too large to include in context.

parameters.file_id: Slack file ID from the uploaded file metadata.
parameters.query: Keyword or phrase to search. If omitted, returns the beginning excerpt.
parameters.limit: Maximum matching excerpts. Defaults to 5, max 20.

slack-json_analyze.description: Analyze an uploaded Slack JSON file structurally without putting the full file into context. Use for statistics, field distributions, numeric summaries, and group-by analysis.

parameters.file_id: Slack file ID from uploaded file metadata.
parameters.group_by: Optional top-level or dotted field path to group records by.
parameters.metrics: Optional numeric field paths to summarize. Auto-detected when omitted.
parameters.top_fields: Optional categorical field paths for top value counts. Auto-detected when omitted.
parameters.limit: Maximum top values or groups to return. Defaults to 10, max 50.

slack-send_screenshot.description: Upload the latest Playwright browser screenshot to the current Slack thread. Only call this when the user explicitly asks to see a screenshot AND pw-screenshot has already been called in the current Playwright flow. Do not call this speculatively or outside a Playwright automation context.

parameters.data_uri: Leave empty to use the screenshot from the last pw-screenshot call (recommended). Only set if you have a specific data URI to upload.
parameters.filename: Optional filename for the uploaded file (e.g. login-page.png). Defaults to screenshot.png.

web-search.description: Search the public web and return results with titles, URLs, and snippets. Use for current external information not available in Slack, code, or runbooks.

parameters.provider: Optional provider override: brave, duckduckgo, searxng, google_cse, or serpapi. Defaults to configured WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER.

web-read_page.description: Read a public web page and return extracted title, URL, and readable text. Use when the user provides a URL, after web-search returns a promising result, or when you already know a stable source URL and search failed or is unnecessary.

parameters.url: Absolute http or https URL to read.
parameters.max_chars: Maximum extracted text characters. Defaults to 12000, max 50000.

luckin-query_shop_list.description: Query nearby coffee stores by location. Use before product search or ordering.

luckin-search_product.description: Search products in a store from the user's natural-language query. Use after choosing a store.

luckin-switch_product.description: Switch a product option such as temperature, size, sugar, or ice level. Use product attribute IDs returned by product search or detail.

luckin-query_product_detail.description: Query product details and selectable attributes for a store product.

luckin-preview_order.description: Preview a pickup order, including estimated price, applicable coupons, and items. Always call this before creating an order.

luckin-query_coupons.description: Query applicable coupons and discounts for the selected store and products. Coupon codes from the response can be passed to create_order.

luckin-create_order.description: Create an order after previewing it and validating all required order details. The server applies the configured automated action policy. If a payment QR code URL is returned, show it as the primary payment option.

parameters.couponCodeList: Optional coupon code list from preview.

luckin-query_order_detail.description: Query order status and pickup details.

luckin-cancel_order.description: Cancel an order. Only call when the user explicitly asks to cancel.

pw-navigate.description: Open a web page in the headless browser. Use this to access and test a live web application — login pages, dashboards, staging environments, etc. After navigation the tool waits for page state to settle and automatically switches back from about:blank popups when possible. Typical flow: pw-navigate → pw-snapshot → pw-click/pw-type → pw-snapshot or pw-screenshot.

pw-snapshot.description: Read the current page structure as an accessibility tree. Returns structured text listing all interactive elements (buttons, inputs, links) with refs like [ref=s1e4]. Always call this after pw-navigate to understand what's on the page, and use the refs for pw-click/pw-type. Do NOT try to read .playwright-mcp/* file paths from the output — they live inside the browser container and are not accessible from the workspace.

pw-click.description: Click an element on the page. Get the ref from a pw-snapshot result (e.g. [ref=s1e4]). Use for buttons, links, checkboxes, etc. The tool waits for navigation/display state to settle after the click and auto-recovers focus from about:blank popups when possible.

parameters.ref: Element reference from the accessibility snapshot (e.g. s1e4).
parameters.target: Deprecated alias for ref; prefer ref.

pw-type.description: Type text into an element. Use for input fields, search boxes, login forms, etc. Get the ref from pw-snapshot. The tool waits for navigation/display state to settle after typing.

parameters.target: Deprecated alias for ref; prefer ref.
parameters.text: Text to type into the element.

pw-fill_form.description: Fill multiple form fields at once. Use for login forms or complex forms with multiple inputs. Each field needs a ref from pw-snapshot.

parameters.fields: Array of field objects, each with: ref (element ref from snapshot), element (human-readable description), name (field label), type (textbox/checkbox/radio/combobox/slider), value (value to set).

pw-screenshot.description: Capture a screenshot of the current browser page inside a Playwright automation flow. Before capture, the tool checks page focus and auto-recovers from about:blank popups when possible. The image is stored internally — you will NOT receive the image data directly. Call slack-send_screenshot afterward only when the user explicitly asks to see the screenshot.

parameters.type: Image format: png or jpeg. Optional, defaults to png.
parameters.fullPage: Set to true to capture the full scrollable page instead of just the viewport.
parameters.filename: Optional filename hint for the screenshot.

pw-press_key.description: Press a keyboard key. Use after pw-type to submit forms (Enter), switch focus (Tab), or dismiss dialogs (Escape). The tool waits for navigation/display state to settle afterward.

parameters.key: Key name (e.g. Enter, Tab, Escape, ArrowDown).

pw-wait.description: Wait for something to happen on the page — either for specific text to appear/disappear or for a time delay. Use after navigation or clicks that trigger loading.

parameters.text: Text to wait for on the page.
parameters.textGone: Text to wait for to disappear.

pw-evaluate.description: Evaluate a JavaScript expression in the browser context. Use for tasks that can't be done with click/type — reading computed styles, checking localStorage, inspecting DOM state. Runs in the browser (not Node.js), so use standard browser globals like document, window, localStorage.

parameters.expression: JavaScript expression to evaluate, e.g. "document.title" or "localStorage.getItem('token')" or "document.querySelectorAll('a').length".

pw-get_all_pages.description: List all open browser tabs/pages. Returns tab index, title, and URL for each open tab. Use this when pw-navigate lands on about:blank (OIDC popup), when you need to know which tabs are open, or before calling pw-switch_page.

pw-switch_page.description: Switch focus to a different browser tab by its index. Use after pw-get_all_pages to switch from an about:blank popup back to the main page, or to navigate between multiple open tabs.

parameters.index: Tab index to switch to (integer from pw-get_all_pages output, e.g. 0 for the first tab).

k8s-get_pods.description: List Kubernetes pods with status, restart counts, and node placement. Use for quick cluster health checks or to find pods for further investigation with k8s-logs or k8s-describe.

parameters.namespace: Kubernetes namespace. Defaults to K8S_DEFAULT_NAMESPACE. Pass explicitly to query a different namespace.
parameters.label_selector: Label selector filter, e.g. app=my-service or app.kubernetes.io/name=gateway.
parameters.field_selector: Field selector, e.g. status.phase=Running or spec.nodeName=node-1.
parameters.all_namespaces: If true, list pods across all namespaces.
parameters.context: kubectl context name to override the default. Use to query a different cluster, e.g. gke_project_region_cluster-name.

k8s-describe.description: Describe a Kubernetes resource showing events, conditions, and configuration details. Use for investigating pod crashes, pending states, or misconfigured resources.

parameters.resource: Resource type: pod, deployment, service, node, ingress, configmap, hpa, job, cronjob, statefulset, daemonset, etc.
parameters.name: Resource name. If omitted, describes all resources of this type.
parameters.context: kubectl context name to override the default. Use to query a different cluster.

k8s-logs.description: Fetch container logs from a Kubernetes pod. Faster than GCP Cloud Logging for real-time debugging. Supports previous container logs for crash investigation. Pass a label selector (e.g. app=my-service) in the pod field to stream logs from all matching pods.

parameters.pod: Pod name (e.g. my-pod-abc12) or label selector value (e.g. app=my-service). If the value contains '=', kubectl logs -l is used automatically.
parameters.container: Container name within a multi-container pod.
parameters.tail: Number of recent log lines. Defaults to 100, max 2000.
parameters.previous: If true, fetch logs from the previous terminated container instance (crash investigation).
parameters.grep: Case-insensitive text filter applied to log lines after retrieval.
parameters.timestamps: If true, include timestamps in log output.
parameters.context: kubectl context name to override the default. Use to query a different cluster.

k8s-top.description: Show resource usage (CPU and memory) for pods or nodes via kubectl top. Requires metrics-server. Use for capacity planning or spotting resource pressure.

parameters.resource: One of: pods, nodes. Defaults to pods.
parameters.name: Optional specific pod or node name.
parameters.namespace: Kubernetes namespace (pods only). Defaults to K8S_DEFAULT_NAMESPACE.
parameters.containers: If true, show per-container resource usage (pods only).
parameters.context: kubectl context name to override the default. Use to query a different cluster.

slack-create_canvas.description: Create a Slack Canvas with structured Markdown content. Use only when the user asks for a canvas/document, or when the result is too long or too structured for a normal Slack reply, such as post-mortems, incident reports, runbooks, decision records, migration plans, or multi-section investigation summaries. Do not use for ordinary short answers, status updates, or simple bullet lists. The canvas is attached to the current channel by default.

parameters.title: Canvas title.
parameters.markdown: Canvas content in Slack Canvas Markdown. Good fits include headings, paragraphs, checklists, ordered/unordered lists, code blocks, links, and simple tables. Avoid raw HTML, Mermaid, images, interactive widgets, or layouts that require precise visual positioning.
parameters.channel_id: Optional channel ID to attach the canvas to. Defaults to current conversation channel.

tts-speak.description: Convert text to natural speech using MiMo-V2.5-TTS and send the audio message to the current Slack thread. Supports multiple voices and style control for expressive speech. Use when the user asks you to speak, read aloud, or when voice output enhances the experience.

parameters.text: Text to synthesize into speech. Place in assistant role — this is what gets spoken.
parameters.voice: Voice name. Built-in voices: 冰糖 (female, Chinese), 茉莉 (female, Chinese), 苏打 (male, Chinese), 白桦 (male, Chinese), Mia (female, English), Chloe (female, English), Milo (male, English), Dean (male, English). Defaults to 冰糖.
parameters.style: Optional natural language style instruction. Examples: 'warm and cheerful tone, moderate pace' or 'calm bedtime story narrator voice'. Placed in user role to guide speech style.

k8s-events.description: List Kubernetes events sorted by last-seen timestamp. This is the first tool to reach for when a pod is CrashLooping, stuck in Pending, or failing to schedule — events show scheduler decisions, image pull failures, OOMKilled reasons, and liveness probe failures before they appear in logs.

parameters.all_namespaces: If true, show events across all namespaces.
parameters.for_object: Filter events for a specific object name, e.g. a pod or deployment name.
parameters.reason: Filter by reason field, e.g. BackOff, OOMKilling, FailedScheduling, Pulled, Started.
parameters.type: Filter by event type: Warning or Normal. Omit to see both.
parameters.context: kubectl context name to override the default. Use to query a different cluster.

k8s-rollout.description: Check rollout status or history of a Kubernetes workload. Use status to verify a deployment is progressing or complete after a release; use history to see revision changelog and spot when a regression was introduced.

parameters.name: Deployment, StatefulSet, or DaemonSet name.
parameters.kind: Workload kind: deployment (default), statefulset, or daemonset.
parameters.revision: For history action, show details for a specific revision number.
parameters.context: kubectl context name to override the default. Use to query a different cluster.

k8s-get.description: General-purpose kubectl get for any Kubernetes resource type: deployment, service, ingress, configmap, hpa, job, cronjob, statefulset, daemonset, node, pv, pvc, namespace, etc. Use k8s-get_pods for pod-specific output. Secrets are blocked.

parameters.resource: Resource type, e.g. deployment, service, ingress, hpa, job, cronjob, node, pvc.
parameters.name: Optional resource name. If omitted, lists all resources of this type.
parameters.all_namespaces: If true, list across all namespaces.
parameters.output: Output format: wide (default), yaml, json, name, or jsonpath=...
parameters.context: kubectl context name to override the default. Use to query a different cluster.

gcp-run_services.description: List or describe Cloud Run services in a GCP project. Use list to see all deployed services, their URLs, and last-deploy times; use describe to inspect a specific service's configuration, traffic splits, and container settings.

parameters.project: GCP project. Defaults to configured GCP_PROJECT.
parameters.region: Cloud Run region. Defaults to configured GKE_REGION.

gcp-run_revisions.description: List Cloud Run service revisions to audit deployment history or investigate a traffic split. Shows revision name, creation time, serving status, and container image digest. Useful for confirming which revision is live after a deploy or rolling back investigation.

parameters.service: Service name filter. If omitted, lists revisions across all services.
parameters.project: GCP project. Defaults to configured GCP_PROJECT.
parameters.region: Cloud Run region. Defaults to configured GKE_REGION.

gcp-clusters.description: List or describe GKE clusters in a GCP project. Use list for a high-level overview of all clusters (status, version, node count, region); use describe for full configuration of a specific cluster.

parameters.project: GCP project. Defaults to configured GCP_PROJECT.
parameters.region: GKE region. Defaults to configured GKE_REGION.
parameters.zone: GKE zone (for zonal clusters). Takes precedence over region.
